html:
Gia Long, born Nguyễn Ánh in 1762, was the founder of the Nguyễn dynasty, the last dynasty of Vietnam, and the first ruler of all its present lands.

He was a teenager when the Tây Sơn killed most of his family. For twenty-five years he fought back from the far south, at times in exile in Siam, helped by the French bishop Pigneau de Behaine, who raised a few volunteers and ships. He took Hanoi in 1802 and took the reign name Gia Long.

He made Huế his capital and, in 1804, adopted the name Việt Nam for the country. He ruled on Chinese lines, with a new law code and Confucian exams. His heirs were hostile to French missionaries, which France later used as an excuse for the conquest of Cochinchina. The Nguyễn emperors reigned until 1945.
